## Natural history notes

A microscopic freshwater green alga belonging to the desmids, characterized by relatively large, flattened cells divided into two symmetrical semicells with deeply incised margins. Euastrum pinnatum has five-lobed semicells, broad expanded apical lobes, and conspicuous lateral indentations that give the cell a somewhat pinnate or feathered outline. It occurs primarily in acidic, nutrient-poor freshwater habitats such as bog pools, moorland ponds, and other oligotrophic wetlands. Like many desmids, it is strongly associated with low-nutrient, acidic waters and can serve as an indicator of relatively undisturbed freshwater conditions.
